Nicknamed the 'Knight King' or 'Soldier King' for his role in World War I, this Belgian monarch succeeded his uncle Leopold II to the throne in 1909 — who was he?
Albert I of Belgium (8 April 1875 - 17 February 1934) was King of the Belgians from 23 December 1909 until his death in 1934.
Born in the colonial Carolinas and married to Rachel Donelson, this Army general turned seventh U.S. president lent his name to a whole democratic movement — who is he?
Andrew Jackson (March 15, 1767 - June 8, 1845) was the seventh president of the United States from 1829 to 1837.
Married to Benazir Bhutto in 1987, this politician later served two separate terms as Pakistan's president, decades apart — who is he?
Asif Ali Zardari (born 26 July 1955) is a Pakistani politician who has served as the 14th president of Pakistan since 2024.
George Washington trusted this major general enough to hand him command of West Point — which he then schemed to surrender to the British in 1780. Who was the would-be turncoat?
Benedict Arnold was British military officer (1741–1801).

A former Unilever executive who rose to CEO of Air New Zealand, he became leader of the Opposition in 2021 and prime minister two years later — who is he?
Christopher Luxon (born 19 July 1970) is a New Zealand politician and businessman who has served as the 42nd prime minister of New Zealand since 2023.
Nicknamed the 'King of the Wild Frontier,' this American frontiersman represented Tennessee in the U.S. House of Representatives before dying while fighting in the Texas Revolution — who is he?
Davy Crockett (August 17, 1786 - March 6, 1836) was an American politician, militia officer and frontiersman.
Followers of this modern movement pick careers and donate to charities based on rigorous cost-benefit calculations, aiming to maximize positive impact worldwide — what movement is this?
Effective altruism (EA) is a 21st-century philosophical and social movement that advocates impartially calculating benefits and prioritizing causes to provide the greatest good.
This former guerrilla movement, born from a 1980 merger of leftist Salvadoran factions, later became a political party after El Salvador's long civil war ended in 1992 — which group?
Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front is a Salvadoran left-wing political party and former guerrilla rebel group.
Speaking a Continental Celtic language and bearing the hallmarks of La Tène culture, this Iron Age people spread across what is now France, Belgium, and beyond — who were they?
Gauls (Ancient) were a group of Celtic peoples of mainland Europe in the Iron Age and the Roman period (roughly 5th century BC to 5th century AD).

Schooled in exile in the US and Argentina after his party's founder was ousted, he came home to lead the opposition coalition against a military dictatorship — and served as Panama's president from 1989 to 1994. Who was he?
Guillermo Endara (May 12, 1936 - September 28, 2009) was a Panamanian politician who served as the president of Panama from 1989 to 1994.
Cast off Mount Olympus by his mother due to a congenital impairment, this Greek god presided over fire, metalworking, and volcanoes — who is he?
Hephaestus (eight spellings; Ancient) is the Greek god of artisans, blacksmiths, carpenters, craftsmen, fire, metallurgy, metalworking, sculpture, and volcanoes.
Known to the Romans as Somnus, this Greek god of sleep is the namesake behind a word for an induced trance — who is he?
Hypnos (Ancient), also spelled Hypnus, is the personification of sleep.
This criminal-defence lawyer represented Bramalea—Gore—Malton in Ontario's legislature before leading a major Canadian federal party from 2017 to 2025 — who is he?

Jagmeet Singh (born January 2, 1979) is a Canadian politician and lawyer who served as the leader of the New Democratic Party (NDP) from 2017 to 2025 and as the member of Parliament (MP) for Burnaby South from 2019 to 2025.

Having left school at 13 to join Melbourne's labour movement, this Labor leader served as Australia's prime minister through most of WWII's Pacific war and is often ranked among the nation's greatest — who was he?
John Curtin (8 January 1885 - 5 July 1945) was an Australian politician who served as the 14th prime minister of Australia from 1941 until his death in 1945.
This politician represents the Sircilla constituency in the Telangana Legislative Assembly and was named Most Inspirational Icon of 2015 by a major Indian broadcaster — who is he?
K. T. Rama Rao (born 24 July 1976), commonly known as KTR, is an Indian politician and Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) of Telangana Legislative Assembly.
This American politician served as South Dakota's governor before becoming the eighth U.S. secretary of homeland security in 2025 — who is she?
Kristi Noem (NOHM; ne Arnold; born November 30, 1971) is an American politician serving as the United States special envoy for the Shield of the Americas since 2026.
Before becoming the 28th U.S. secretary of defense, this retired Army general was the first African American to command U.S. Central Command — who is he?
Lloyd Austin (born August 8, 1953) is a retired United States Army general who served as the 28th United States secretary of defense, from 2021 to 2025, under the Biden administration.
Born into the House of Valois in Lorraine, this queen consort of Henry VI became a driving force of the Lancastrian cause in the Wars of the Roses — who is she?
Margaret of Anjou (23 March 1430 - 25 August 1482) was Queen of England by marriage to King Henry VI from 1445 to 1461 and again from 1470 to 1471.
A poet and broadcaster who entered politics through the Labour Party, this Irishman served as mayor of Galway before becoming president of Ireland from 2011 to 2025 — who is he?
Michael D. Higgins (born 18 April 1941) is an Irish politician, poet and broadcaster who served as the president of Ireland from November 2011 to November 2025.

This Indian lawyer and Indian National Congress leader served as party president from 1919 to 1920 and again from 1928 to 1929, and fathered the man who would become independent India's first prime minister — who is he?
Motilal Nehru (6 May 1861 - 6 February 1931) was an Indian lawyer, activist, and politician affiliated with the Indian National Congress.
Before becoming France's president in 2007, this Paris-born politician served as mayor of Neuilly-sur-Seine and led the UMP party — who is it?
Nicolas Sarkozy (sar-KOH-zee; born 28 January 1955) is a French former politician who served as the president of France from 2007 to 2012.

This American showman built fame on celebrated hoaxes and co-founded a legendary circus — though he insisted the cynical phrase 'there's a sucker born every minute' was wrongly pinned on him — who was he?
P. T. Barnum (July 5, 1810 - April 7, 1891) was an American showman, businessman, and politician remembered for promoting celebrated hoaxes and founding the Ringling Bros.
The fifth Roman governor of Judaea under Tiberius, he's named in both the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds — and is even venerated as a saint by the Ethiopian Orthodox Church. Who is he?
Pontius Pilate was the fifth governor of the Roman province of Judaea, serving under Emperor Tiberius from 26/27 to 36/37 AD.
Nicknamed 'electric brain' for his calm under pressure, this U.S. admiral commanded Task Force 16 at Midway, where American dive bombers sank four Japanese fleet carriers — who was he?
Raymond A. Spruance (July 3, 1886 - December 13, 1969) was a United States Navy admiral during World War II.

Sparked in 1917 amid wartime bread shortages and battlefield defeats, this upheaval abolished a monarchy and installed a socialist government after two successive uprisings and a civil war — what is it called?
Russian Revolution was a period of political and social change in Russia, starting in 1917.
This liberal, pro-European Ukrainian party takes its name from a sitcom starring the man who'd go on to become the country's real president — which party?
Servant of the People (SN) is a liberal, centrist, pro-European political party in Ukraine.
This ruler quelled a rebellion in Gdańsk and worked closely with chancellor Jan Zamoyski during his decade as king of Poland — who was he?

Stephen Báthory (27 September 1533 - 12 December 1586) was King of Poland and Grand Duke of Lithuania as well as Prince of Transylvania (1576-1586), after previously being Voivode of Transylvania (1571-1576).
This German politician has co-chaired the far-right Alternative for Germany party since 2019 alongside Alice Weidel, and is known for pro-Russian, eurosceptic foreign-policy views. Who is he?
Tino Chrupalla (born 14 April 1975) is a German politician from the far-right party Alternative for Germany (AfD).
After heading the Soviet gas ministry, this man became Gazprom's first chairman, then Russia's Prime Minister for six years during the transition from a planned to a market economy — who is he?
Viktor Chernomyrdin (9 April 1938 - 3 November 2010) was a Soviet and Russian politician and businessman.
Praised for strategy but condemned for scorched-earth tactics against the Confederacy, this Ohio-born Union general from a politically prominent family graduated West Point in 1840 — who was he?
William Tecumseh Sherman (tih-; February 8, 1820 - February 14, 1891) was an American businessman, author, and United States Army general in the Union Army during the American Civil War (1861-1865).

Battle of Khaybar: 628 military campaign in the early Muslim period.

Charan Singh: Prime Minister of India from 1979 to 1980. Singh was principally known for his land and agricultural reform initiatives, and was Member of Parliament (MP) for Baghpat.

This ancient Athenian orator first took the stand at age 20 to win back his inheritance from his own guardians, before becoming a professional speechwriter and, by 354 BC, a political voice — who is he?
Demosthenes: Classical Athenian statesman and orator (384–322 BC)

A former tanner and shipowner from Le Havre, this politician became France's seventh president in 1895 and died suddenly in office four years later — who was he?

Serving as Chief Minister of Assam since 2021, this politician switched from the Congress party to the BJP in 2015 and has represented Jalukbari in the state assembly six times — who is he?

Himanta Biswa Sarma: Chief Minister of Assam since 2021. Himanta Biswa Sarma (born 1 February 1969) is an Indian politician and lawyer serving as the 15th and the current Chief Minister of Assam since 2021.
Serving as prime minister across three separate periods spanning nearly four decades, this politician is Cambodia's longest-serving head of government — who is he?
Hun Sen: Prime Minister of Cambodia (1985–1993; 1998–2023)

Isaac: Biblical patriarch, son of Abraham and Sarah. Isaac first appears in the Torah, in which he is the son of Abraham and Sarah, the father of Jacob and Esau, and the grandfather of the twelve tribes of Israel.

Kais Saied: President of Tunisia since 2019. As president, Saied has overseen democratic backsliding, as he has repressed the political opposition and dissidents in Tunisia.
On May 2, 2011, SEAL Team Six carried out Operation Neptune Spear at a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan, ending a manhunt that began with the war in Afghanistan — what event was this?
Killing of Osama bin Laden: 2011 U.S. military operation in Abbottabad, Pakistan.
In Arthurian legend, this enchantress figure gifts Excalibur to the king, raises the knight Lancelot, and later helps carry the dying king to Avalon — who or what is she?
Lady of the Lake: Sorceress in Arthurian legend. As either single character or multiple ones, the figure of the Lady of the Lake often appears in various roles in the works of modern culture.

Shaped by liberal ideas and the non-aggression principle, this political philosophy prizes liberty and personal sovereignty above all, holding you may live as you choose so long as you don't force or defraud others — what is it?
Libertarianism: Political philosophy based on liberty. Different categorizations have been used to distinguish these various forms of libertarianism.
A Burma Campaign veteran regarded as the founder of the Bangladesh Armed Forces, he served as commander-in-chief of the Bangladesh Forces in 1971 — who was this four-star general?
M. A. G. Osmani: Bangladeshi military general & revolutionary (1918–1984)

Pechenegs: Extinct Turkic people. The Pechenegs or Patzinaks, were a semi-nomadic Turkic people from Central Asia who spoke the Pecheneg language.

Head of the Catholic Church for nearly 32 years — the longest verified reign in history — this pontiff convened a council that defined papal infallibility before declaring himself a 'prisoner' after Rome's capture in 1870 — who was he?
Pope Pius IX: Head of the Catholic Church from 1846 to 1878.
A war correspondent in Afghanistan and Angola in the 1980s, this Oxford-educated Polish statesman later became his country's Foreign Minister and, since 2025, also Deputy Prime Minister — who is he?

This early American writer gave us 'Rip Van Winkle' and 'The Legend of Sleepy Hollow,' and later served as the U.S. ambassador to Spain — who was he?
Washington Irving: American writer, historian and diplomat (1783–1859)

Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md (formerly Mv) and atomic number 101.
In what year was Stephen Hawking born?
Stephen Hawking: Hawking was born in Oxford into a family of physicians.
In what year did Isaac Newton die?
Isaac Newton: Newton contributed to and refined the scientific method, and his work is considered the most influential in bringing forth modern science.
In what year was Potassium discovered?
Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
SEPECAT Jaguar: Breguet Aviation. As of 2026, the Jaguar remains in service with only the Indian Air Force.
Which country is Curtiss P-40 Warhawk from?
Curtiss P-40 Warhawk: United States. The Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.
Who is credited with discovering Palladium?
Palladium: William Hyde Wollaston. Palladium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Pd and atomic number 46.
Who is credited with discovering Pectin?
Pectin: Henri Braconnot. The principal chemical component of pectin is galacturonic acid (a sugar acid derived from galactose).
Who is credited with discovering Oxygen?
Oxygen: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
The simplest alkyne, this colorless gas owes its straight-line shape to a carbon-carbon triple bond — and though pure it's odorless, commercial grades reek thanks to impurities. What is it?
Acetylene (systematic name: ethyne) is a chemical compound with the formula C2H2 and structure HCCH.
This Indian economist won the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his work on welfare economics and has also studied the causes of famines — who is he?
Amartya Sen (born 3 November 1933) is an Indian economist and philosopher.
Found only on male deer, except reindeer, this branching structure of bone and cartilage falls off and regrows from scratch each year — what is it?
Antler are extensions of an animal's skull found in members of the Cervidae (deer) family.
Caused by poor circulation, lost nerve supply, or simple disuse, this process shrinks a cell, organ, or tissue below its normal mature size — what's it called?
Atrophy is the partial or complete wasting away of a part of the body.

Known only from larval and juvenile specimens until video footage of much larger adults surfaced, this deep-sea cephalopod genus holds its long, elbow-like arms perpendicular to its body — what is it?
Bigfin squid are a group of rarely seen cephalopods with a distinctive morphology.
This flowering plant family is known for flowers with four petals arranged in a cross shape, and includes crops ranging from leafy greens to root vegetables to condiment seeds. Name the family?
Brassicaceae (the older but equally valid) Cruciferae is a medium-sized and economically important family of flowering plants commonly known as the mustards, the crucifers, or the cabbage family.

Spread through contact with infected feces and capable of killing up to 91% of untreated cases, this highly contagious virus mainly strikes dogs and wolves but can also infect foxes, cats, and skunks — what's the virus?
Canine parvovirus (also referred to as CPV, CPV2, or parvo) is a contagious virus mainly affecting dogs and wolves.

The only living member of its genus, this big cat sprints at up to 104 km/h thanks to powerful hindlimbs, long legs, and a flexible spine, and wears black tear-like streaks down its face; which animal is it?
Cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) is a species of large feline and the only living member of the genus Acinonyx.

Native to western South America, this shrub bears oval leaves and red berries, and when its leaves are chewed or brewed as tea they act as a mild stimulant with no evidence of addiction — which plant is it?
Coca refers to any of the four cultivated plants in the family Erythroxylaceae, native to western South America.
Native to North America and smaller than its close relative the gray wolf, this canine fills a similar ecological niche to the golden jackal of Eurasia — which animal?
Coyote (Canis latrans) is a species of canine also known as the American jackal, prairie wolf, and brush wolf.
Defined as having at least three loose or watery bowel movements in a day, this common condition can quickly cause dehydration, especially in children. What condition is it?
Diarrhea (American English), also spelled diarrhoea (British English), is the condition of having at least three loose, liquid, or watery bowel movements in a day.
This English physician created the world's first vaccine, targeting smallpox, and in doing so coined the very term 'vaccine' — derived from the Latin for 'pustules of the cow.' Who was he?
Edward Jenner (17 May 1749 - 26 January 1823) was an English physician and scientist who pioneered the concept of vaccines and created the smallpox vaccine, the world's first vaccine.
The major female sex hormone, this estrogen steroid drives the development of breasts and a female pattern of fat distribution and regulates the menstrual cycle — which one is it?
Estradiol (E2), also called oestrogen, oestradiol, is an estrogen steroid hormone and the major female sex hormone.

Sometimes mistakenly called a cat despite belonging to the weasel family, this North American forest-dwelling carnivore is the only living species in its genus and is larger than the martens it resembles — what animal is it?
Fisher (animal) (Pekania pennanti) is a carnivorous mammal native to North America, a forest-dwelling creature whose range covers much of the boreal forest in Canada to the northern United States.

The first person in Germany to hold a professorship dedicated to experimental physics, he is remembered for his posthumous 'waste book' notebooks and for the tree-like electrical discharge patterns named after him. Who is he?
Georg Christoph Lichtenberg (1 July 1742 - 24 February 1799) was a German physicist, satirist, and Anglophile.
This branch of medicine focuses on the female reproductive system, and when combined with the study of pregnancy and childbirth forms the field known as OB-GYN — name the specialty?
Gynaecology (or gynecology in American English) is the area of medicine concerned with conditions affecting the female reproductive system.

First described by an English physician in 1832, this cancer of the lymphocytes is identified by giant multinucleated Reed-Sternberg cells in the lymph nodes, and about half its cases trace back to the Epstein-Barr virus. What is it?
Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is a cancer where multinucleated Reed-Sternberg cells (RS cells) are present in the lymph nodes.

Forming at or below zero degrees Celsius, this naturally occurring crystalline solid is technically classified as a mineral and appears on Earth, other planets, and even in interstellar space — what is it?
Ice is water that is frozen into a solid state, typically forming at or below temperatures of 0 C, 32 F, or 273.15 K.
Trained in biochemistry and physiology before ranging into geography and anthropology, this American author won the 1998 Pulitzer for Guns, Germs, and Steel — who is he?
Jared Diamond (born September 10, 1937) is an American scientist, historian, and author.

This childhood illness of unknown cause mainly affects kids under five, causing a prolonged fever lasting more than five days that doesn't respond to typical fever-reducing medicine, plus inflamed blood vessels throughout the body — name the syndrome?
Kawasaki disease (also known as mucocutaneous lymph node syndrome) is a syndrome of unknown cause that results in a fever and mainly affects children under 5 years of age.
With about 180,000 described species — roughly 10% of all known living organisms — which insect order is the second largest, trailing only the beetles?
Lepidoptera are an order of winged insects which include butterflies and moths.
Serving under Chancellor Adenauer, this economist championed West Germany's postwar economic miracle before becoming chancellor himself in 1963 — who is he?
Ludwig Erhard (4 February 1897 - 5 May 1977) was a German politician and economist who served as the second chancellor of West Germany from 1963 until 1966.
The heaviest and largest members of the squirrel family, these 15 species of grazing ground-dwellers vanish each winter to hibernate underground — what are they?
Marmot are large ground squirrels in the genus Marmota, with 15 species living in Asia, Europe, and North America.

An advanced modification of the Korean War-era MiG-15, this Soviet transonic fighter jet entered production in 1952, was license-built in both China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — what's the aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17 (NATO reporting name: Fresco) is a transonic fighter aircraft that was produced in the Soviet Union from 1952 and was operated by air forces internationally.
Lacking a cell wall entirely, this tiny bacterial species causes a form of atypical lung infection linked to cold agglutinin disease — which microbe first isolated as the 1944 'Eaton agent'?
Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a species of very small-cell bacteria that lack a cell wall, in the class Mollicutes.
Sold in packs needing a desiccant to keep it from absorbing moisture, this seaweed sheet was once used as currency and shrine offerings in Japan — what is it?
Nori is a dried edible seaweed used in Japanese cuisine, usually made from species of the red algae genus Pyropia, including P. yezoensis and P. tenera.
Part of the Bovidae family, this genus of seven social species is better known simply as sheep, all thought to trace back to the wild mouflon — which genus?
Ovis is a genus of mammals, part of the Caprinae subfamily of the ruminant family Bovidae.

Which American chemist was the first to synthesize physostigmine and pioneered making progesterone and testosterone from plant sterols — even starting a company to extract steroid intermediates from wild Mexican yams?
Percy Lavon Julian (April 11, 1899 - April 19, 1975) was an American research chemist and a pioneer in the chemical synthesis of medicinal drugs from plants.
This zodiac sign's Latin name means 'fishes,' and it's where the ecliptic crosses the celestial equator near the March equinox — which one?
Pisces (constellation) is a constellation of the zodiac. It is between Aquarius, of similar size, to the southwest and Aries, which is smaller, to the east.

Caused by a mutation in a single gene that holds the cell nucleus together, this rare disorder makes children age much faster than normal, with most patients living only into their teens or twenties — what's the condition?
Progeria (also Hutchinson-Gilford syndrome or Hutchinson-Gilford progeroid syndrome; HGPS) is a type of progeroid syndrome.

Cultivated mainly for its oil-rich seeds, this yellow-flowered Brassica crop is the source of a low-toxicity oil marketed under a Canadian-coined name, and ranks as the world's third-largest vegetable oil source — what is it?
Operating under a pseudonym borrowed from The Princess Bride, this American created the first modern darknet marketplace before his 2013 FBI arrest — who is he?
Ross Ulbricht (born March 27, 1984) is an American cybercriminal who created and operated Silk Road, the first modern darknet market, from 2011 until his arrest in 2013.
Most episodes of this brain-activity disruption last under two minutes and leave the person confused or fatigued afterward, but one lasting over five minutes is a medical emergency — what is it?
Seizure is a sudden disruption of brain activity caused by excessive, synchronized neuronal firing that results in changes in behavior.
With the formula Na2CO3, this odorless white salt yields an alkaline solution in water and earned the name 'soda ash' because plant ashes once gave it up. What is it?
Sodium carbonate (also known as washing soda, soda ash, sal soda, and soda crystals) is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates.

Harvested from the seeds of the nux-vomica tree, this bitter colorless alkaloid is infamous as a poison for rodents and birds — yet was once doled out in tiny doses to stimulate the heart and bowels. What is it?
Strychnine (-nin, US chiefly -nyne) is a highly toxic, colorless, bitter, crystalline alkaloid used as a pesticide, particularly for killing small vertebrates such as birds and rodents.
A colorless, water-miscible cyclic ether and a versatile solvent, this compound is mainly used as a precursor to polymers and is an isomer of butanone — what is it?
Tetrahydrofuran (THF), or oxolane, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2)4O.

A phenylpiperazine compound in the serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor class, this antidepressant treats depression, anxiety and insomnia but carries a rare risk of prolonged, painful erections — which drug?
Trazodone is an antidepressant medication used to treat major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, and insomnia.
Once classified in the honeysuckle family before molecular studies gave it its own, this genus of 150-plus shrub species reaches Africa only via the Atlas Mountains — which genus?
Viburnum is a genus of about 150-175 species of flowering plants in the family Viburnaceae.

This Greek economist served as Finance Minister under PM Alexis Tsipras during the 2015 debt crisis, becoming internationally known for opposing EU-imposed austerity, before co-founding the left-wing party DiEM25 — who is he?
Yanis Varoufakis (born 24 March 1961) is a Greek economist, academic, author, and politician.
Also called sweet flag, this wetland plant contains psychoactive compounds and has been banned from American food products despite centuries of use in traditional medicine — which species?
Acorus calamus: Species of plant. Acorus calamus (also called sweet flag, sway or muskrat root, among many other common names) is a species of flowering plant with psychoactive chemicals.
This congenital condition causes a total or partial absence of pigment, leading to white hair, pale skin, and often pink or reddish eyes — what is it called?
Albinism: Disorder causing lack of pigmentation.
Despite being named after a European bird for its reddish-orange breast, this thrush is the most abundant landbird on its continent, numbering some 370 million individuals — what is it?
American robin: Species of bird. The American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.

A German pharmacist coined this pigment's name from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue' in 1835 — it shifts red to purple to blue depending on pH and colors blueberries, black rice, and autumn leaves; what is it?
A notoriously toxic metalloid and pnictogen with atomic number 33, it's used in lead alloys for car batteries and ammunition and as a semiconductor dopant — which element is it?
Arsenic: Chemical element with atomic number 33 (As). It is a metalloid and one of the pnictogens, and therefore shares many properties with its group 15 neighbors phosphorus and antimony.
The world's largest nocturnal primate, this Madagascar lemur has ever-growing rodent-like teeth and taps tree trunks with a bony middle finger to fish out grubs by echo — which animal?
Aye-aye: Species of primate. This foraging method is called percussive foraging, and takes up 5–41% of the aye-aye's foraging time.
Named after a barberry-related plant genus and glowing bright yellow under ultraviolet light, this alkaloid was recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text around 200 BC. What compound is it?
This North American wild cat earns its name from the black-tipped, stubby tail it sports, along with distinctive black bars on its forelegs — one of the four species of lynx. Which animal is it?
Bobcat: Medium-sized North American wild cat.

Best known for his role as Ben Hunter in a soapy prime-time revenge drama, this American actor also starred as Will Davis on The CW's 'Privileged' and Kyle Parks on Lifetime's 'The Client List.' Who is he?
Its dihydrate form is the mineral gypsum and its dehydrated cousin is bassanite; sparingly soluble, it causes permanent hardness in water — which inorganic salt is this?
Calcium sulfate: Chemical derived from gypsum used in food and industry.
A nerve compression syndrome caused when the median nerve in the wrist becomes compressed, causing numbness and tingling in the thumb and fingers. What is this condition?
Carpal tunnel syndrome: Compression of the median nerve in the wrist. It can also be measured with electrodiagnostic tests.
India's third lunar mission carried a lander named Vikram and a rover, both replacing equivalents lost when the previous mission crashed on landing. What was the rover called?

Chandrayaan-3 is the third mission in ISRO's Chandrayaan lunar-exploration programme, consisting of the lander Vikram and the rover Pragyan, replacements for the equivalents on Chandrayaan-2, which crashed on landing.
In this chronic liver condition, healthy tissue is replaced by scar tissue and regenerative nodules, choking blood flow and causing portal hypertension — what is it called?
Cirrhosis: Chronic disease of the liver, characterized by fibrosis.
In mathematics, this is a selection of items from a set where the order of choosing them does not matter, unlike a permutation — what is it called?

Combination: Selection of items from a set. In mathematics, a combination is a selection of items from a set that has distinct members, such that the order of selection does not matter (unlike permutations).
Domesticated in Africa and thriving in sandy, low-rainfall soil, this ancient legume is now grown mostly in Nigeria and Niger, which together supply two-thirds of the world's crop — which plant?
Cowpea: Species of plant. The cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna.
Son of a bass-baritone and born into a family of engineers, this American built his first car at 19, won four F1 Grands Prix, and took Le Mans in 1967 — who was he?
Dan Gurney: American racing driver, engineer and motorsport executive (1931–2018)
This colorless, highly flammable liquid with a sweet smell was once widely used as a general anesthetic before modern alternatives — what compound?
Defined in humans as an adult height of four foot ten or shorter, this condition's most common form — accounting for about 70% of cases — is a genetic disorder called achondroplasia. What is it?
Dwarfism: Small size of an organism, caused by growth deficiency or genetic mutations.
This Italian-American physicist discovered two elements, technetium and astatine, plus the antiproton — the last earning him a share of the 1959 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was he?
Emilio Segrè: Italian-American nuclear physicist and radiochemist (1905–1989)
Marketed under brand names like Arcoxia, this selective COX-2 inhibitor developed by Merck was approved in 63 countries by 2007 — everywhere, notably, except the United States — what is the drug?
This membranous bodily structure comes in superficial, visceral, and deep types, and a dangerous pressure buildup within it can cause compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Fascia: Layer of connective tissue in the body.

Members of this insect order have just one pair of true wings — the hindwings evolved into balance organs called halteres — and the group includes mosquitoes among its 150,000+ species. What are they commonly called?
Fly: Order of insects. A fly (pl. flies) is an insect of the order Diptera (from Ancient Greek δι- di- 'two' and πτερόν pteron 'wing'), named for the single pair of wings.
Caused by a loss of blood supply and marked by skin turning red or black, this condition comes in dry, wet, and gas forms — what is it?
Gangrene: Type of tissue death by ischemia.

Inducted into the U.S. Air Force Hall of Fame in 2018, this American mathematician modeled the precise shape of the Earth — work later baked into the Global Positioning System that now guides your phone. Who is she?
Designed specifically for airborne early warning rather than adapted from an existing airframe, this twin-turboprop carrier plane replaced the piston-engined Tracer for the US Navy — which aircraft?
Grumman E-2 Hawkeye: Airborne early warning and control aircraft. The Northrop Grumman E-2 Hawkeye is an American all-weather, carrier-capable, tactical airborne early warning (AEW) aircraft.
Spiny like a porcupine but actually a distant cousin of the shrew, this nocturnal little mammal comes in 17 species across Europe, Asia, and Africa — and was introduced to New Zealand; what is it?
Known as the great apes, this primate family holds eight living species across four genera — orangutans, gorillas, chimps and bonobos, plus one more: us. What is it?
Hominidae: Family of primates. The original meaning of "hominid" referred only to humans (Homo) and their closest extinct relatives.

Responsible for nearly half a million deaths each year, this condition occurs when the body produces or absorbs more heat than it can dissipate, most often from heat stroke or a drug reaction — what condition?
Hyperthermia: Elevated body temperature due to failed thermoregulation.
Covering patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets, this legal category of intangible creations first developed as a concept in 17th- and 18th-century England — what is it called?
Intellectual property: Ownership of creative expressions and processes.
A French soldier turned naturalist, this early proponent of biological evolution published the three-volume 'Flore françoise' and joined the French Academy of Sciences in 1779 — who is he?
Nicknamed 'Iron Annie,' which corrugated-skin transport plane began life as a 1930 civilian airliner before Nazi Germany converted it for military use?
Situated between two larger folds of skin, these paired flaps extend from the inner vaginal and urethral openings and form the clitoral hood above — which structures are these?
Labia minora: Flaps of skin on either side of the vaginal opening in the vulva.
Cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, growth and reproduction are its hallmarks — and every instance of it eventually reaches death. What capacity in matter is this?

This Canadian physicist worked on the Manhattan Project determining critical mass values for uranium and plutonium, and in 1946 was fatally exposed to radiation in a lab accident at Los Alamos — who is he?
Louis Slotin: Canadian physicist and chemist (1910–1946)
Nicknamed sea cows, these slow-moving herbivorous mammals graze on more than 60 kinds of aquatic plants in the Caribbean, the Amazon basin, and West Africa — what are they?
Manatee: Genus of mammals. The main causes of death for manatees are human-related issues, such as habitat destruction and human objects.
This cone-shaped part of the brainstem controls involuntary functions from sneezing to heart rate, and was once known simply as 'the bulb' — which structure?
Medulla oblongata: Structure of the brain stem.
This branch of economics studies how individual firms and consumers allocate scarce resources, as opposed to the economy-wide view of its counterpart — which field?
Microeconomics: Behavior of individuals and firms.
First prepared in 1908 by biochemist Kikunae Ikeda as he tried to bottle the savory taste of kombu seaweed, this flavor enhancer is the original source of umami in cooking — what is it?
Monosodium glutamate: Flavor enhancer (621 or E621)

This inner-ear condition brings on episodes of vertigo, ringing in the ears, and hearing loss lasting anywhere from 20 minutes to several hours — believed to stem from fluid buildup in the labyrinth. What is it?
Ménière's disease: Disorder of the inner ear. The hearing loss and ringing in the ears can become constant over time.
Its name literally means 'blue cow,' though only the males actually sport a bluish-grey coat — which is the largest antelope species in Asia?
A Boston physician, medical reformer, and 'fireside' poet, this polymath delighted readers with his 'Breakfast-Table' series begun in 1858. Who was he?
Oliver Wendell Holmes Sr.: American poet, essayist, physician (1809–1894)
With long dense grey fur and rounded ears set oddly low on the sides of its head, this small wild cat — first described in 1776 near Lake Baikal — roams the cold steppes of Central Asia. What is it?
Pallas's cat: Species of small wild cat. Pallas's cat (Otocolobus manul), also called manul, is a small wild cat with long and dense light grey fur, and rounded ears set low on the sides of the head.
This bony ring connects the spine to the lower limbs at the hip joints, formed by the sacrum, coccyx, and a pair of hip bones — what body region?
Pelvis: Lower torso of the human body.

So reactive that it never appears uncombined in nature, this element was famously isolated in 1669 by Hennig Brand — the scientific community's first documented discovery of an element — and comes in white and red forms. Which one is it?
Phosphorus: Chemical element with atomic number 15 (P)
With a half-life of just 138 days, this rare radioactive element occurs only in trace amounts within uranium ore and is chemically similar to selenium — what is it?
Polonium: Chemical element with atomic number 84 (Po)
Genetic studies trace this most widely cultivated apricot species to Central Asia, though its scientific name nods to a country in the Caucasus — what is it?
Prunus armeniaca: Species of apricot. The native range is somewhat uncertain due to its extensive prehistoric cultivation.
About the size of a house cat, this nocturnal herbivorous marsupial thrives on Rottnest Island near Perth and is the only member of its genus — what is it?
Quokka: Small marsupial from southwestern Australia.

Covering more than 200 conditions from arthritis to soft-tissue pain syndromes, this umbrella term for chronic joint and connective-tissue pain gives its name to a whole medical specialty — what is it called?
Rheumatism: Medical conditions affecting the joints or connective tissue.
Known as 'swede' in British English, this root vegetable is a hybrid of cabbage and turnip — what is it?
Rutabaga: Root vegetable in the Brassica family.
Named from Greek words for 'thorn' and 'earthworm,' which genus of large tropical centipedes gives its name to an entire family of segmented, many-legged predators?
Named for its enormous footwear-shaped beak, this large wading bird of East African swamps was once classified with storks but is now grouped with pelicans and herons — what is it?
Shoebill: Species of bird. The shoebill (Balaeniceps rex), also known as the whale-headed stork, whalebill, and shoe-billed stork, is a large long-legged wading bird.
After designing the BBC Micro and its BASIC, this English computer scientist co-created the instruction set for ARM — now the most widely used processor architecture in smartphones. Who is she?
Common in coastal tropical waters worldwide, this group of cartilaginous fish includes about 220 species across 29 genera, from butterfly rays to manta and devil rays — what are they?
Its explosive yield became the standard yardstick for comparing bombs and even asteroid impacts; chemists also use it to make charge-transfer salts — what's this nitro compound?
Discovered via its telltale green spectral line in 1861, this silvery post-transition metal takes its name from the Greek word for a green shoot — which element?
Thallium: Chemical element with atomic number 81 (Tl)
Covered in taste buds and divided into oral and pharyngeal parts, this muscular mouth organ also helps clean the teeth and enable speech — what is it?
Tongue: Muscular organ in the mouth of most vertebrates.
Nicknamed the "immortal jellyfish," this tiny sea creature can revert from a sexually mature adult back into an immature, sea-floor-dwelling polyp stage instead of dying — what species is it?
Turritopsis dohrnii: Species of small, biologically immortal jellyfish.
Commonly called the guelder-rose, this Old World flowering shrub belongs to the Viburnaceae family — what's its scientific name?
Viburnum opulus: Species of flowering plant.
This form of hypertext publication is collaboratively edited and managed by its own audience, working directly through what?
A wiki is a form of hypertext publication on the internet which is collaboratively edited and managed by its audience directly through a web browser.

Born in New York City, this Irish statesman commanded Volunteers at Boland's Mill during the 1916 Easter Rising, narrowly avoided execution due to his American citizenship, and later authored the 1937 Constitution — who is he?
The symbol for copper is Cu. Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu and atomic number 29.

In what year was Kiefer Sutherland born?
Kiefer Sutherland: Kiefer William Frederick Dempsey George Rufus Sutherland (born 21 December 1966) is a British and Canadian actor.
In what year was Gene Hackman born?
Gene Hackman: Eugene Allen Hackman (January 30, 1930 – February 18, 2025) was an American actor.
In what year was Maggie Smith born?
Maggie Smith: Dame Margaret Natalie Smith (28 December 1934 – 27 September 2024) was a British actress.
In what year was Alexis Bledel born?
Alexis Bledel: Kimberly Alexis Bledel ( blə-DEL; born September 16, 1981) is an American actress and model.
In what year was Seth Rogen born?
Seth Rogen: Seth Aaron Rogen ( ROH-gən; born April 15, 1982) is a Canadian actor, comedian, filmmaker, and cannabis entrepreneur.

Emilia Clarke: Clarke's television debut was a guest appearance in the BBC One medical soap opera Doctors in 2009, at age 22.

Brie Larson: Brianne Sidonie Desaulniers (born October 1, 1989), known professionally as Brie Larson, is an American actress, singer and filmmaker.

Samantha Ruth Prabhu (born 28 April 1987) is an Indian actress who works predominantly in Telugu and Tamil films.

Dustin Hoffman: Dustin Lee Hoffman (born August 8, 1937) is an American actor and filmmaker.
In what year was Park Seo-joon born?
Park Seo-joon: Park Yong-kyu (Korean: 박용규; born December 16, 1988), better known by the stage name Park Seo-joon (박서준), is a South Korean actor.
In what year was Prince born?
Prince Rogers Nelson (June 7, 1958 – April 21, 2016), known mononymously as Prince, was an American singer, songwriter, musician, dancer, actor, and filmmaker.
In what year did Matthew Perry die?
Matthew Perry: Matthew Langford Perry (August 19, 1969 – October 28, 2023) was an American and Canadian actor.
In what year did Chadwick Boseman die?
Chadwick Boseman: Chadwick Aaron Boseman (November 29, 1976 – August 28, 2020) was an American actor and playwright.
In what year was The Pale Blue Eye first released?
The Pale Blue Eye is a 2022 American period mystery gothic thriller film written and directed by Scott Cooper, adapted from the 2006 novel by Louis Bayard.
In what year was The Woman King first released?
The Woman King is a 2022 fictionalised historical drama depicting the Agojie, the all-female regiment in the West African Kingdom of Dahomey.
In what year was The First Slam Dunk first released?
The First Slam Dunk: It is based on Inoue's Slam Dunk manga series.
In what year was E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial first released?
E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (or simply E.T.) is a 1982 American science fantasy film produced and directed by Steven Spielberg and written by Melissa Mathison.
In what year was Big Hero 6 first released?
Big Hero 6 is a 2014 American animated superhero film loosely based on the superhero team from Marvel Comics.
